ideas.title: Should you bring that broken vase? — A householder's guide to Eastmere's ceramics repair table
ideas.description: Practical preview for local householders: how to book a fifteen-minute assessment (10:00–13:00), the walk-in policy, the types of ceramics the team will look at (decorative items such as vases and figurines), the exclusion of eating/drinking ware because adhesives are not food‑contact certified, that the assessment is free, and what repair outcomes to expect (volunteers will discuss appearance and material contribution; some items may show visible seams or be left unrepaired).
ideas.audience: Householders in Eastmere who are wondering whether a broken decorative ceramic is worth bringing to the community hall session.
ideas.rationale: The notice explicitly addresses householders deciding whether to bring broken objects and lists operational details and likely outcomes, so an explanatory preview will directly meet stated reader need and set realistic expectations for the event (which is the collective's first ceramics table and has no prior ceramics metrics).
ideas.evidence: The assessment is free; volunteers will discuss likely appearance and the material contribution with the owner before doing any work; some objects will leave with visible seams; some will leave unrepaired.

ideas.title: From bikes to bowls: Eastmere repair collective’s first ceramics table
ideas.description: A short community profile about the collective expanding from bicycle sessions to a first ceramics table, highlighting volunteer-run services and how this new offering differs (types accepted, safety limits, and no prior ceramics outcome figures).
ideas.audience: Local readers interested in community initiatives and volunteer-run repair projects.
ideas.rationale: The switch from bicycle sessions to a first ceramics table is a clear change in activity and has neighborhood interest, but the source provides limited operational detail and no outcome data, so the piece would be an explanatory profile rather than an impact evaluation.
ideas.evidence: The collective has held bicycle sessions before, but this is its first ceramics table.

ideas.title: What to expect at Eastmere’s ceramics table — quick checklist
ideas.description: A short FAQ/checklist for people planning to attend: booking a 15-minute slot (10:00–13:00), walk-ins only if slots free, bring only decorative ceramics (vases, figurines), do not bring eating/drinking vessels (adhesives not food‑contact certified), assessment is free, and repairs may leave visible seams or may not be done.
ideas.audience: Attendees and prospective attendees who need quick practical instructions before traveling to the event.
ideas.rationale: The notice lists several simple, actionable rules and expectations (booking policy, item types accepted, safety exclusion, cost, and outcomes) that translate directly into a concise checklist readers can use immediately.
ideas.evidence: People may book a fifteen-minute assessment between 10:00 and 13:00; walk-ins will be seen only if a booking slot is free. The team will look at decorative ceramics such as vases and figurines. It will not accept objects used for eating or drinking, because its adhesives are not certified for food contact.

grounding.claim: The editorial should be a timely, practical guide tied to the event (ceramics table opening on 21 November).
grounding.sourceEvidence: The Eastmere repair collective will open a ceramics table at the community hall on 21 November.
grounding.inference: The quoted sentence identifies an event (a ceramics table) and its date and location, which supports producing a timely guide framed around that opening.
grounding.constraints: The sentence gives event type, date and place but does not specify all operational details or audience needs; those must be drawn from other sentences in the source.

grounding.claim: The piece should explain booking (fifteen-minute assessments 10:00–13:00), walk-in policy, the team’s focus on decorative ceramics (vases, figurines), and the exclusion of eating/drinking ware because adhesives are not food‑contact certified.
grounding.sourceEvidence: People may book a fifteen-minute assessment between 10:00 and 13:00; walk-ins will be seen only if a booking slot is free. The team will look at decorative ceramics such as vases and figurines. It will not accept objects used for eating or drinking, because its adhesives are not certified for food contact.
grounding.inference: These contiguous sentences lay out operational details (booking length and window, walk-in rules), the accepted object types, and the explicit safety-based exclusion, which justify including those points in the description.
grounding.constraints: The sentences state the rules but do not quantify capacity (how many slots), nor explain alternative options for excluded items; also they do not describe repair techniques or costs beyond the assessment being free.

grounding.claim: The target readers are local householders wondering whether a broken object is worth bringing.
grounding.sourceEvidence: Its notice is for householders wondering whether a broken object is worth bringing.
grounding.inference: The sentence explicitly names 'householders' and their question as the intended audience and purpose of the notice, supporting a guide aimed at that group.
grounding.constraints: The source names householders but does not segment them further (e.g., by age, mobility, or prior repair experience), so audience framing should stay general and local.

grounding.claim: A preview that sets expectations is timely because this is the collective's first ceramics table and there are no prior ceramics outcome figures.
grounding.sourceEvidence: The collective has held bicycle sessions before, but this is its first ceramics table. It has no figures yet for ceramics repaired, objects diverted from disposal, or the life of a repair.
grounding.inference: These contiguous sentences establish novelty (first ceramics table) and a lack of metrics on outcomes, which together justify an explanatory piece to set expectations rather than an evaluation of impact.
grounding.constraints: The sentences do not explain why ceramics outcomes differ from bicycle sessions or how volunteers will track future metrics; they only establish absence of current figures.

grounding.claim: The notice says the assessment is free, volunteers will discuss likely appearance and material contribution before doing any work, and some objects may leave with visible seams or unrepaired.
grounding.sourceEvidence: The assessment is free. If the volunteers think a repair is feasible, they will discuss the likely appearance and the material contribution with the owner before doing any work. Some objects will leave with visible seams; some will leave unrepaired.
grounding.inference: These contiguous sentences provide direct operational and outcome facts (cost = free; consent/discussion before work; possible visible seams or no repair), which can be cited as concrete points in the editorial to set reader expectations.
grounding.constraints: The sentences state these outcome possibilities but do not quantify how often repairs are feasible or how visible seams correlate with longevity; they do not include adhesive safety (covered elsewhere).
